utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We can then follow the chronological order, and we are coming to the incident in Kaonik in May 1992. As you have already told the Court, on the 2nd of April, 1992, the crisis staff of the municipal assembly of Busovaca was set up. It consisted of ten members, and you were the chairman or the head of that crisis staff; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you ran the affairs and life in the municipality in view of the threat of war which was looming over Bosnia-Herzegovina. But will you tell us, which was the chief task of the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The chief task of the crisis staff was to run the municipality in wartime conditions. That was the general task. Because in the territory, or the municipality of Busovaca, there were three barracks: at Kacuni, Draga, and Kaonik. This crisis staff intended to organise the activities about the evacuation of the Yugoslav People's Army and to carry it to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, we are being warned to slow down and to make breaks, to make pauses between question and answer, so shall we try to do that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: It's not only your fault; it's also mine. Now, briefly, very briefly, was there any negotiation between the Muslim and the Croat community in Busovaca who would take which barracks, in view of the location of each of these barracks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Indeed, there were negotiations, and we reached an understanding at a meeting of the crisis staff that the Kacuni barracks, which was evidently in an area with the Muslim population, that it should be given over for management to the Muslim part. And the barracks at Draga, which was located in the territory of the Croat population, it was agreed that its armaments and the management over it should be given to Croats. The Kaonik barracks, which was four kilometres away, in the direction of Zenica, four kilometres from Busovaca, in the direction of Zenica, at Travnik, it was located amidst the Croat majority. But it was agreed then that the armaments in the barracks should be distributed 50/50.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us, please, as the negotiations about the dislocation of JNA from Busovaca were going on, or rather when the Draga barracks in Busovaca was evacuated on the 26th of April, 1992, is also the day when the JNA bombed the town of Busovaca, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 26th of April -- and that was Easter, the little Easter, as we call it -- Busovaca was bombed at 1920. In that attack, three persons were killed: a Muslim, a Croat, and a little 14-year-old Croat girl. Buildings were on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. I do not think we have to go into detail; we just want to draw a general picture. This business about the evacuation of the troops from the Draga barracks, this business was headed by Mr. Glavocevic on behalf of the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The crisis staff appointed Mr. Florijan Glavocevic and Husein Hadzimejlic to conduct negotiations and see about the evacuation of the Yugoslav People's Army. So they were the two men responsible for the evacuation of the barracks; barracks, I mean first, second, and third barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Because of the bad experience with the Draga barracks, I suppose there were negotiations about their pull-out from the Kaonik barracks. These negotiations were conducted much more carefully, if I may put it that way. Could you briefly tell us, how did these negotiations go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: As for negotiations about the evacuation of the Kaonik barracks, it was agreed that it would be evacuated and that the weaponry which was in it, that it should be distributed equally between the Bosniak Muslim and the Croat people. However, as this distribution was underway -- and before that, I had a crisis staff meeting, and everything was agreed how we would proceed about this, and from that meeting I went to the Kaonik barracks with Mr. Niko Grubesic, and then the troops were -- the troops of the Yugoslav People's Army were already set to go. They were all lined up and we were waiting for them to be able to go out so that we could jointly -- Florijan and Hadzimejlic should then try and split up what there was to split up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Sorry I butt in, but I wanted to say it was precisely because the JNA was in the barracks. Will you tell us, please, where was the control point of the HVO? How far from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: It was some 250 metres from the barracks, the control point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And why was it put up?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The reason for it was to prevent the movement of their units and to supervise the comings and goings from the barracks, because I had also received reports. And it is on record. I can check that. I can check my conversation with Mr. Tomislav Sipcic, which took place in Zenica, and where before that there had been a major theft of weaponry, because that is where the weapons of the Busovaca Territorial Defence were stored. So that a theft had also taken place, so that we had to monitor who was entering and leaving the Kaonik barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And tell us, the place where this supervision, where this control point, Sendolin Bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is Sendolin Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who are the people living there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: They are predominantly all Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And tell us, while you were in the barracks, did you hear anything happening outside?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: I was in the barracks and I heard a rifle shot. There was a shot. And I can say that at that moment the members of the Yugoslav People's Army took their positions, that is, they all leapt into their trenches. And at that moment I was informed that an incident had taken place at this control point, that a Croat and a Muslim had been wounded. And when this gunfire, when this incident happened, we then immediately stopped everything. We said that the Yugoslav People's Army would not leave that place. And then Mr. Glavocevic and Mr. Hadzimejlic came to me and said that in the discotheque called Leptir, a largeish group of able-bodied persons, Muslims, headed by Mr. Merdan, Dzemal, wanted to simply enter the Kaonik barracks so that they could take over all those weapons themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please: The understanding about the division of weapons between the Muslims and Croats in Busovaca, that was an understanding reached at the local level, municipal local level; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Indeed, because the crisis staff, this staff, as it was called then, took all decisions at their meetings only with regard, in relation, to the relevant municipality, that is, people of the municipality concerned. So that we had reached that understanding, and Mr. Dzemal Merdan, he was the commander of the Territorial Staff, of the Territorial Defence, quartered in the municipality of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This arrival of large numbers of military -- of the Muslims, what was supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: He was there trying to take over the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In the end, Mr. Maric, who was to blame, which side was to blame for the breach of agreement which you reached in Busovaca municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzemal Merdan is the guilty party because he wanted to take over these weapons in a forcible way. This created mistrust in relation to me and Mr. Hadzimejlic because it was never part of the agreement that Mr. Merdan would come with his soldiers to take over those weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, we should slow down. I believe that one answer was not fully interpreted. In addition to Mr. Merdan, who came from Zenica, were there local commanders from the Patriotic League or Territorial Defence who were involved in this breach of agreement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of the Busovaca Patriotic League, Mr. Dervis Sarajlic, also known as Gica, was involved. That was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you remember any other name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Alija Begic was also there. He was the commander of the Patriotic League, but I don't know what rank he held.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This is why this agreement could not be implemented, for which Mr. Florijan Glavocevic and Mr. Husein Hadzimejlic were responsible.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, this agreement could not be implemented, and I requested that the crisis staff meet again so that we could discuss the issue again. However, that night, this was around 8.30 p.m., the representatives of the Bosnian Muslims did not want to come, they refused, and we made an agreement about what to do with those weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we give an exhibit to the witness to see. It's Z100. I prepared a copy and it can be given to the witness to look at, with the permission of the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: A little while ago, Mr. Maric, you said that you had certain information that weapons were stolen from the Kaonik barracks. Did you have any reports that those weapons were being sold to one of the sides?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. You should know that weapons could have been taken only from the JNA, and a blackmarket was created with these weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that that night a meeting of the crisis staff was supposed to have taken place but it never did, and then you, and I assume the Croat members of the municipal staff, but you held a meeting in which you tried to find a way out of the situation in which you found yourselves.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, and this is how this order was compiled. It consists of 19 items, and it was signed by the then commander of the municipal staff, Mr. Ivo Brnada, and also it was signed by Mr. Dario Kordic as the HVO vice-president. What I want to say is that the Croatian leadership, headed by myself, compiled this order and it was signed as such. Mr. Dario Kordic was only there to confirm that he was present at the time when the JNA military barracks were vacated from the municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps we can just briefly go through the contents of this document, which was adopted on 10 May 1992. It speaks for itself. We shouldn't burden the Trial Chamber with it, but you brought it up in your evidence so maybe you want to comment on some of these items. If not, we can perhaps just wait for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The order as such, I think, speaks for itself. I think it is clear what it enjoined.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well, then. Let us not go into any details. I assume that there will be questions relating to it. But one of the items refers to the TO and other organisations being placed under the control of the HVO, or they will have to surrender their weapons to the HVO. Was this decision ever implemented?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: That decision was never implemented, because the Territorial Defence, headed by Mr. Hadzimejlic, continued to operate in the Busovaca municipality up until 25 January 1993, which was terrible for us Croats and all people of this territory because it was a day without precedent in the history of the Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, there is also an order that the units which are deployed in the Leptir club, that they surrender to the HVO. Did they ever surrender to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No, they never surrendered to the HVO. They just pulled out. They were let go and they left the area of the Leptir discotheque.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you also say something about the item referring to Merdan, Sarajlic, and Begic? Were they to be arrested and released?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Messrs. Begic and Sarajlic were not arrested. I just know that Mr. Merdan was arrested and then released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you do not know any details about it because you were not involved in it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to add that sometime around 1200 hours I went home because I was fairly sick, so I wasn't there until the very end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask, who would affect the arrest of Merdan, Sarajlic, and Begic? Who would actually arrest them? Which body?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you understand the question of Judge Robinson, Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Dzemal Merdan was arrested by the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Were the others arrested?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The others, from the information I had, were not arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Another item from this document. A temporary curfew was introduced, and "temporary" explains it all, I think, but how long did this curfew last?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: From what I know it only lasted for 72 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were there any other repressive measures taken against the Busovaca population, members of any ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: There was no repression. And Busovaca, according to the census, had 47 per cent Bosniaks and they were never mistreated, just as the Serbs were not in those days, at the time when the curfew was in force.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, the crisis staff, who was the authority at the time, was then disbanded and the HVO decided to take over the functions of government.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. By this order, the crisis staff was disbanded, and I was its head, and the Croatian Defence Council from then on assumed the full authority for the Busovaca territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me, why was the town blocked and why were the transports controlled on the road through Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: You must know that the bombing of the 26th of April by the JNA had created a lot of suspicion, and any movements of the JNA caused a lot of suspicion on the part of the Croat and Muslim population. The first bombing was terrible for us. So the checkpoints were set up in order to prevent the passage of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you simply wanted to control the traffic; you wanted to control all the convoys and the passage of persons and goods.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that the Territorial Defence continued to operate in the Busovaca territory after 10 May 1992. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where the office of the TO commander, Mr. Husein Hadzimejlic, was throughout 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: It was in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Where? In which building?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: In the municipal building, in one part of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In the same building where you worked; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can move on. We're moving to paragraph 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: After several days of further JNA attacks on your territory, you started to get organised and started organising municipal services.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: That is exactly right. The HVO government was organised which wanted to restart the normal life in Busovaca municipality, and things started coming back to normal in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: At the time when you reorganised the administration, could the central government in Sarajevo exercise any influence there in Busovaca? Because at that time the government was besieged by the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: I can say that there was no influence from the central government in Sarajevo because all communication lines were practically interrupted. So we had to rely on ourselves, and together with the Bosnian Muslims we tried to solve all issues which we needed to solve. I need to point out here that the area of Kupres was occupied at the time, and that was the main highway to the coast. So you couldn't use the road through Kupres and we had to look for a way out. We started building a road, which we called "The Road of Salvation," and that was the only way through which we could resupply food stocks and medication which we needed for the population of Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What road was this; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: This was the road Novi Travnik-Pavlovica-Gornji Vakuf, which went on over Mount Vran --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: -- down to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: A moment ago you told the Trial Chamber that the HVO government in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was established in August. But looking from May on and taking into account all of the HZ HB, was there a distinction between the HVO-HDZ in Busovaca, or was there still confusion over this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: At first there was confusion. They didn't know what was the military and what was the civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When was this crystallised so that people knew precisely what was the competence of the civilian and what was the competence of the military component?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: When the HZ HB government was established, the civilian HVO and the military part of the HVO started being separated, because the military part then established its main headquarters, it was led by Mr. Milivoje Petkovic, and the civilian part was led by Mr. Prlic. They had its departments, and one of them was for national defence; it had its own minister. So they had ministries which worked and instructed the civilian authorities on what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So your civilian HVO government in Busovaca in the latter part of 1992 relied on this central government of the HVO in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I assume, then, that in this period, that is, the latter part of 1992, the military and the civilian police were separated, that is, their combatants, the two police forces in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The head of the civilian police was appointed and the military police had its own combatants and its own commander, so the civilian and military police were separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: We can move on to paragraph 24. Mr. Maric, who was appointed the head of the civilian government in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was Franjo Kristo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I think we have a misunderstanding. I'm talking about the first HVO government head in Busovaca, not the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The first civilian HVO administration president was Mr. Florijan Glavocevic. And I was appointed as an acting president of the HVO on 1st August 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Naumovski, I think we should try to move on more speedily. I must ask, if Mr. Nice does not have any objections on various paragraphs, perhaps you could be more leading, provided there are no objections to that, in order to speed matters up. Mr. Nice, are there some paragraphs on which you would not be objecting if the witness were led?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think it's unlikely that there are any whole paragraphs that are not paragraphs where matters should be dealt with carefully, because this is a very central and wide-ranging proof, or offer of proof, as it's called. But if there's -- well, if Mr. Naumovski is a little more leading from time to time, I'll stand up and object when I think that we've gone too far. Would that help? It's a little difficult. The paragraphs are far too packed, really, to say, of any paragraph, it can all be led.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Right. So we shall ask you to do that. As you know, we must remember the time. We have one hour yet, so will you try to be as concise as possible and to lead your witness when a paragraph allows you to do so, evidently under the control of the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I didn't want to do this in order to avoid the objections from the Bench opposite, but I will now try to do so that we can speed things up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, you sketched for us how the authority was set up in Busovaca, how you reorganised the administration. And can you tell me whether the civilian HVO or administration which was established and which operated in Busovaca, did it discriminate the Muslim citizens of Busovaca, that is, in comparison to the civilian administration, before the time when the HVO took over?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No. Out of seven local departments, or ministries, three went to the Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So did the same people who worked in the old municipal government continue to work in the new government after the HVO took over?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber whether any employee or head of department in this newly established government had to sign any oath of loyalty or any other kind of oath to anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No one ever had to sign any oath of loyalty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was this introduced as a new kind of feature?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No verbal or written statement of loyalty was ever introduced?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: I never told anyone to sign any statement, because I considered every citizen of Busovaca equal. Anyone who lived in Busovaca municipality, I wanted him to be able to have all the rights that he needed to exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Naumovski, will you ask Mr. Maric if the municipal staff of whatever ethnic origin were all paid in the same way.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody was being paid a salary according to the scales that were established.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps just one additional question. There was a classification of different jobs, and these job were all classified and it had --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every job had its own description. It has its -- and it was made part of the scales, and everybody received salary according to the scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In this reorganisation of government, was anyone dismissed out of all those who were employed in the previous administration?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Nobody in the municipal government was dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And were any positions cancelled?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No. All employees who worked in the municipal government continued to work in their jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I have a specific name. What happened to Mr. Asim Sunulapasic's position? Could he stay with the government? He was the president of the former government. What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The president of the HVO government had the executive power, and according to the organisation, according to the old system, that was the position that was held by the president of the executive board, so that Mr. Sunulapasic was no longer an official, but he was allowed to stay. He was a specialist, an expert in economic affairs, and he was asked to stay. But he decided to go to Vatrostalna, where he had been, and I was with the Sumarija.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You told a while ago that there was no discrimination against Muslims, and you agree with me that there are numerous examples to show that the Muslims took part in decision-making and in political life of the town and municipality of Busovaca, even after May 1992; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, so far the Defence has not produced too many exhibits. However, Mr. Maric personally signed quite a number of documents, and I should like Mr. Maric to be shown these documents so that he could confirm them. And we may also touch upon some of them briefly. Ninety per cent of the documents that we wish to produce were signed by Mr. Maric and he was their author. We already handed over these documents to the registry, so perhaps we could go through them document by document. I believe that would be the speedier way to do that. These are, by and large, very short documents, so could we have English versions on the ELMO and Croat versions shown to the witness. We won't spend too much time on these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be number D241/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, this is an introductory document to facilitate our work. This document is of the 16th of July, 1992. It was signed by the then-president of the HVO, of the Busovaca municipality, Mr. Glavocevic. In a sentence, this document speaks for itself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. One sees that it is ordered that the trading company Tisovac, for private bakery Orman, owned by a Muslim from Kacuni, be issued two tonnes of flour, which of course had to be paid at the valid prices.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. So this is an administrative act, I'd call it. It is an administrative act. It has its number, the date, and so on and so forth. However, some of these papers are entitled "order," some are a so-called decree or certificate, so could that be this wandering around, this uncertainty in the early days, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So when it says "order," it doesn't mean a military order, does it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we can move on to the second document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D242/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, you, I mean Croats and Muslims, cooperated in matters of the school curriculum and the beginning of the school year 1992/1993. From what I can see, and from what I read in this document, the municipal government in Busovaca also cooperated with schools in Kacuni and all other schools in the municipality. This document is of the 31st of July, 1992. In a sentence, you hereby order that the elementary school First of May in Kacuni be approved alone?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We cooperated, and all schools in the municipality of Busovaca were treated equally and received money to pay salaries to all the employees, regardless of whether they were Croats, Bosniak Muslims, Serbs, or Montenegrins. All those who were employed were receiving salaries that were due them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you say the First of May, that is what the school was called, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And tell us, in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca, Muslims and Croats account for 90-something per cent of the population. Hadn't you agreed with the Muslim population that the subject of literature should cover, should encompass, only Muslim and Croat authors rather than only Serb as well, as in the former state; was that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. But if I may, if Your Honours allow me, I should like to simply add that in Busovaca, inhabited mostly by Croats and Bosniaks, who lived and worked in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca, they were taught by -- they were provided instruction mostly by Montenegrins; that is, mostly teachers -- the teachers were Montenegrins and Serbs, and we learnt more about Serb authors than about Croat and Bosniak authors.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Maric. We do not really have to waste the energy of the Court with such detail. I believe the Court has already heard a great deal about this, so we can move on. But since we are discussing literature, did you also have a flexible school policy regarding the curriculum and about subjects such as geography and history?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Everything that expressed history and geography, we agreed that each -- that everyone, in his own language, should instruct his own children in the way that he prefers, that he deems better, in a democratic way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And tell us, please: As for the name of the language, did the Croat and the Muslim side agree about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Croats spoke Croatian, and they in the beginning called it the mother tongue. Because, as you know, under the old system it was Serbo-Croatian, the language of Bosnia and Hercegovina, that is, Croat or Serbian, so that they -- and history proved that. In the plebiscite of 1993, they decided that their language should be called Bosnian, or rather Bosniak, as they prefer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And to round off this set of questions about education, you had also reached an understanding with Muslims in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca to use the school forms which was more to the liking of either group; that is, the Muslims could use forms which they preferred and Croats could use theirs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody had the right to use the forms which they preferred, and they could print the forms in the language they preferred. Nobody forced anything upon anyone, because that was the agreement which was abided by.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can move on with documents. Can we have the third document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D243/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, I forgot, while we were looking at the second document, and again I forgot to ask you. Will you please confirm: You are the author of these documents? I forgot to ask you about that, the previous one and this one.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, this is my signature, my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This document is dated the 6th of August, 1992, and from what I gather from this, you were still part of the payment system in your region, because you write to the public auditing office in Zenica; however, its branch in Busovaca. What was the purpose of this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Let me just explain. Busovaca was at the crossroads. Just to remind the Court, under the previous administrative subdivision it was under the influence of Zenica; rather, it was part of the Zenica region, so that the payments -- the then public auditing service, as it was called then, the territory of Busovaca was also under its jurisdiction. And in the document that you have before you, I address it to the payment service in Zenica, requesting the printing of the coupons, of the notes which were to be used as legal tender in the municipality of Busovaca. Because at that time, in addition to these coupons, we also had a krona, or rather the then Croatian dinar in circulation, and subsequently krona and German mark, so that all these currencies were in circulation both in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we move on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Naumovski, do all these documents bear on the same issue? Do they all bear on the same question, that is, the conduct of the municipal authorities, the management of their affairs in an equitable manner? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have many of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. And also the treatment of the Muslim side. Yes, they are all identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many more documents of this kind do you still have?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at least a dozen or so in this set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Listen, I think you could move on faster because we have grasped what it is all about. I really think you should present all these documents as one and then ask a general question covering all these documents. The witness can identify them. I think we are spending too much time going through these documents individually, so that I think it is better if you have sets of documents, to show them to the witness all as one document and try to move on faster. I believe we have already grasped what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I shall be very happy to abide by the suggestion of Your Honour, but the documents are not identical as regards the areas, the walk of life. We have referred to education which is one subject, and then we have finance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, we understand that, but it is the same issue. So I think you should present all these documents as a set, at one and the same time. We understand what you are talking about, the way in which the municipality was administered, was managed. I do not think we really need to spend too much time on this because we are not here to analyse the municipal administration at the time and go into every detail of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, Your Honour, but could you please tell us, in which way should we proceed? Should they all be marked with one number and then have only subnumbers, slash something? I don't know how technical we need to do it. Perhaps the registrar could help us. How should we mark them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think they can have separate numbers. There is no problem with that. They can still have separate numbers. Yes. Needless to say, the Prosecutor will be entitled to go back to these documents in the course of cross-examination, to go back to all these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We shall try to spend as little time as possible. Can the witness be shown the next document, please. Oh, we already have the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar then please give the whole set of documents to the witness, and then have them introduced. You have the series of documents. Will you please give the whole batch to the witness and then they will be marked as they are produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the number for this first document, and just a very short question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait, Mr. Naumovski. We must ask the registrar to prepare all the remaining documents. They will be numbered immediately and then they will be adduced in a batch.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Your Honours, if I may take the liberty to suggest, perhaps we could make the break now and then I could have it ready with the registrar before we resume in the afternoon. I think we have ten minutes before the break, so perhaps we could break off now. I do apologise. Perhaps I'm taking too much liberty but perhaps it might speed matters up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I would rather that we continue until 1.00. We shall have these all numbered, and I think we can finish this question. We are still at paragraph 26. Could we please move on to paragraph 27. Very well. Could you now give us the number of these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The documents will be numbered D241/1 to D252/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, I presume you understand that every document has now its number, and do not bother about that. Just a sentence in this first document. You are sending this letter to a company called Nigma in Busovaca. Will you agree with me that it transpires from it that every employee, in agreement with a decision of the 30th of April, 1992, employed in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca and nevertheless is engaged in the HVO or TO is entitled to his salary. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So regardless of which armed formation he belongs to.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, regardless of whether he is a member of the HVO or the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We will move on to the next document, which is a document of the 14th of August, 1993. This is your decision to set up municipal departments in the municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Registrar, could we have copies? Could the Judges have copies of the documents, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So it now lists those areas. Will you look at Article 3, please. This was the task of local boards. Could you tell us what that task was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The task of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be better to have these documents on the ELMO, to change these documents on the ELMO. As we go through them, the witness has the documents before him, but can we also go through them on the ELMO? As we move through them, can we also move them on the ELMO? Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar, we marked it as number 5. It is a document bearing our number 5. Or is it perhaps on the ELMO already? Yes, that's the document. Item 3 or Article 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, could it please be moved on the ELMO so we can see Article 3.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Well, the task of local boards was to organise social and economic life on the territory of the area; that is, for every part of the municipality, such branches had to be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This is another one of your documents. You signed this document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This is my document. Only I have to say that it was signed by my secretary, on my behalf, but with my authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The next document, and we see it on the ELMO, this is a press release and you wrote it on the 19th of August, 1992. Two words only. What were the circumstances which resulted in this document prohibiting the disturbance of citizens by gunfire, prohibiting poaching, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: I can say here that because there were already some problems with armament already arriving in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca, that type of peace we had in Busovaca was getting worse. There were poachers and thefts, and I therefore issued a press release prohibiting all the unnecessary activities which could disturb people, because we know how an unnecessary shot can upset somebody, let alone all these things that were happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. This document is of the 26th of January [as interpreted], 1992, and it is another document testifying to the relations between Croats and Muslims at the time. This is your document, addressed to the Assistant Minister of National Defence in Zenica District, and in it you apply for some funds. Now, it shows what was the relationship between these formal bodies of authority in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Will you please look at the second paragraph which, to my mind, is the most telling.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Indeed. Here I ask that equal treatment be accorded to the problem of supply of both the Croat Defence Council and the Territorial Defence, because the HVO had received barely anything -- hardly anything from the central government in Sarajevo, that is, than Zenica district; so that I requested that it be treated equally and to supply in an equal manner all the participants, all the peoples, in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: There seems to be a mistake in the interpretation. The document is of the 26th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The 26th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This document again testifies about the relations not only between Muslims and Croats but also others. The document is of the 1st of September, 1992. You signed it and hereby you authorise, you give your consent for, the operation of the Serb Orthodox Charitable Society of Dobrotvor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document. This is dated the 10th of September, 1992. You signed it, and here you took a decision. These two gentlemen, Abdul Selim Teskeridzic and Dzevad Pripoljac, are designated for a particular job, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Mr. Teskeridzic is a construction engineer; he worked in the municipality of Busovaca. Mr. Pripoljac was a civil engineer, a technician; he also worked in the municipality of Busovaca. And you can see what they were tasked to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, we do not have to go into that. Just a word. They are both Muslims, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. What I want to say is that they both were working.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Next, please. Mr. Maric, this document is one of the 17th of September, 1992. You signed it, and it has the format of a conclusion. Now, items 1 and 2, what do they mean?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Basically they mean that documents may be issued at the request of citizens applying for them, which were about birth, marriages; that they may be issued these forms with their own heading, that is, either Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna or only Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So these are birth certificates, death certificates, school certificates, so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, all those documents which are to be issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Item 2, in point of fact, speaks about the responsibility of workers concerned if they failed to comply with what it says in item 1.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you wish, we can go on, but it seems to me that the time has come for our usual break. But it is, of course, up to you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many more of these documents do you still have, Mr. Naumovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not getting the interpretation. I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many more of these documents do you still have, Mr. Naumovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Eleven in this particular set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then we shall make our break now and we shall resume after one hour and 40 minutes. I will have to ask you to speed up, to expedite the browsing of these documents, because they all bear on the same issue. We are really not here to examine in detail how the municipality of Busovaca was administered. Thank you very much. The session is adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.05 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, Mr. Naumovski. I would like to give the registry the floor now. Could we hear from the registry all the numbers so that we can very precisely know.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- admitted by the Defence will be numbered D241/1 to D261/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that you all have these documents and that the numbers were correctly assigned. So Mr. Naumovski, I count now on your cooperation so that we go straight to the core of the matter. I know that these matters are important and these documents are important for the Defence, so I'm not going to try and prevent you to submit them to the witness, but having said that, I would like you to go straight to the most important topic and try to avoid any -- being too long on anything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that we really will not spend a lot of time on it. We will run through these documents very quickly, the author of which was Mr. Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And Mr. Maric, to get immediately to the point, the next document is a document dated 24 September 1992, D251/1, a decision signed by you regarding setting up of joint patrols to prevent unauthorised logging, and it was to be equally composed of the HVO and the TO.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And this is another document that testifies to the cooperation even when it's about logging?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please, D252/1, another decision, dated 15 October 1992. This is when the crime rate started increasing, and you're directing the civilian police and telling them what their tasks were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We needed to restore law and order in the area, so the police imposed compulsory business hours to restaurants and bars, and were fining those who were in breach of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Next document, please, 253/1. And another decision, not signed by you, but you recognise it as your own. You can see just part of the seal. It has to do with the beginning of the school year. This is the 1992/1993 school year.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I, in fact, issued an order that the military formation of the ABiH in the village of Putis is ordered to vacate the premises in the regional elementary school so that the school children could start using the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So it had to do with the beginning of the school year?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Next document, 254/1, a longer document, dated 2 November 1992. This is November 2nd. A decision on establishing municipal commission for receiving, housing and taking care of displaced persons and refugees of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Due to the operations of JNA in the territory of and the army of Republika Srpska, caused an influx of refugees, and I decided to set up a commission which would be dealing with all the problems relating to the displaced persons and refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Just one question. On the list of people who were appointed as members of this commission, you see that this was a joint commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a mixed commission, composed of both ethnic Croats and Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you can see that under 5, 6, 7, 8, and 13, these members are Muslim.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can name them name by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You don't have to. Let's go to the next document, 255/1, a document dated 4 November 1992 in which you designate a replacement for Mrs. Alima Besic, the head of the lands -- of the office of land survey and property rights of Busovaca, because of her sick leave?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Abdul Selim Teskeridzic replaced her and was appointed as acting head of the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: They are both Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are both Muslims, and we needed to find a Muslim to replace a Muslim head of the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Next document, 256/1, also dated 4 November 1992, that is, end of 1992. Again, appointments. Under 3, clerk Zuhra Rizvic is appointed clerk for statistical data in the fields of agriculture, water resources, and hunting. And what was her ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: She was also an ethnic Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Next document, 257/1, dated 12 November, 1992. This is your order, Mr. Maric, in which you request of the commanders of the military police of the HVO, as well as the ABiH military police and the forestry administration, to step up their patrols.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The unauthorised logging continued and increased so I had to issue such an order to bring this to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So these were joint patrols in the middle of November 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Both Muslims and Croats operated in concert in the territory of Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Next document, 258/1, another document you compiled, dated 27 November 1992. A working body was established. Could you tell us, what was this commission and who were the members?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: It was a joint commission, mixed composition. Marko Pezer, Nezir Huseinspahic, and Abdul Selim Teskeridzic, the last two were ethnic Muslims, they were to tackle the problem of the town dump. This problem we still actually have to date. It has not been resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned that these two gentlemen were Muslims. We have heard in this case that some Muslims who were still employed with the municipal government were there only formally but that they really did not come to work.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No. These gentlemen came to work; I can confirm that, and also they themselves can confirm this. Mr. Nezir Huseinspahic is still with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Next document, 259/1, from the very end of 1992. This is 22 December 1992. Could you please tell us, what kind of a decision was this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: This is a one-time decision for the financial aid to the families of killed soldiers of the HVO and ABiH in the amount of 100 German marks per family, and a list was provided of those who were killed. Also, in addition, 400 kilogrammes of flour was to be distributed, 25 kilogrammes per family. This was as relief to the victims of war because the war had already spread all through the municipality of Jajce, and the units were involved in the defence of the municipalities of Travnik and Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Unfortunately we do not have the list which you mentioned, but we can agree that the HVO, the local Busovaca HVO government, in the end of December 1992, allocated financial aid to families of both HVO and ABiH soldiers who were killed in action.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I mentioned. There was no discrimination. The families of soldiers from both formations who were killed were provided this aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Next document, D260/1. You did not sign it, but I would just like you to tell us about this company called Niskogradnja. They had a branch in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Senad Ekmedzic was its manager, a Muslim. You see a receipt. The managers provided aid to their assistants, to their units, including cigarettes and other items. You can see that any manager in the municipality, regardless of whether he was an ethnic Croat or Muslim, could give such aid to different troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This assistance was given to the 333rd Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The last one in this batch is 261/1. This is an invitation to a meeting, which you sent out on January 8, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had problems with the Sumarija Busovaca company due to the war conditions. I organised a meeting in order to try to resolve these problems in Sumarija Busovaca. I invited representatives of both the Croats and Muslims so that we could tackle these problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You called both political and military representatives?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, because we had a serious problem there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: We can move right ahead, Mr. Maric; that is, go back to the outline --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Naumovski, but once these documents are going to be submitted to the witness -- we see that these documents, for the most part, concern 1992 and they deal with cooperation between Croats and Muslims in the municipality of Busovaca. Mr. Maric, has this cooperation continued in 1993? Because the last document that we were presented with was dated the 8th of January, 1993. Has the cooperation continued? Please go on.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: The cooperation continued until 21 January 1993, when the situation in the Busovaca municipality deteriorated after the checkpoint at Kacuni incident. We attempted to resolve this problem in a peaceful, democratic way. However, on the 24th of January, 1993, in the afternoon, two HVO policemen were killed, Messrs. Ivica Petrovic and a taxi driver named Bogdanovic from Kiseljak. On that day the situation deteriorated, and on the 25th of January, 1993, at 5.30 a.m., the aggression of the Muslim forces began in the territory of Busovaca municipality, and that's when the situation deteriorated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Maric. What happened with the administration of your municipality? Because I see that you remained president up until the spring of 1994. Did you continue to administer your municipality? What was your relations with the Muslims at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: As a representative and the president of the Croatian Defence Council, I attempted to establish contacts with the Bosniak side. However, during 1993 these contacts started being reestablished in February so that we continued to have exchanges in 1993. From February until the 15th of April, 1993, we continued to try to talk and agree that no more incidents be created, because we also signed a ceasefire in February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: We shall reach these subjects that you just mentioned in no time. But we've already broached some of these subjects in paragraphs 27, 28, and 29, so perhaps there's no need to go back to those. Again, just one thing. Is it true that you Croats changed the street names unilaterally?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: We never changed street names unilaterally. In the town of Busovaca it was changed jointly, so as a street was called after a priest and another street was named after an Islamic leader in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you say jointly, you're referring to 1991, after the elections.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, after the elections in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This Court has already had ample opportunity to hear about the arrival of refugees, so on and so forth. So perhaps just a figure. In 1992, how many Serbs, in your view, left Central Bosnia and passed through Busovaca, towards the territory held by the army of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is difficult to speak about all those facts if one looks at what was happening in the territories of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But if I look -- if I cast my eye and my mind back to the territories of the municipalities of Travnik, Busovaca, Zenica, 35.000 -- 30.000, at least, to 35.000 Serbs left. Perhaps even more. Those were column after column. That was a horrible sight, and only a man who saw that can speak about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You can look at the next document, D262/1.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The usher will help you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have all these numbers here, and will you please distribute them, yes, to avoid any misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The following documents will be numbered D262/1 to D274/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, again a document of yours, of 11th November 1992. Only Article 1, in one sentence, for the Court. Apparently there were some individuals, residents of Busovaca, who were requesting to leave; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. As they were leaving the territories or municipalities, the Serbs of ethnic origin, so they asked to leave the territory of the municipality of Busovaca. And on the 11th of November, 1992, I issued them with this document so that they could leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So these are people who wanted to leave of their own free will, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Of course. We never tried to chase anyone away from the territory of the municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please: Is there any truth in the claim that Mr. Kordic, and then the HVO, and I suppose you, as the president of the government, that you charged every family, that is, every person of Serb origin who went through Busovaca in the direction of the territory held by the Bosnian -- by the army of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No, we did not charge anyone. We did not charge anything, regardless of what ethnicity the person leaving the territory of Busovaca belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. We already heard about that from the previous witness, so there is no need to broaden the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are moving to the next paragraph, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, the Court has already heard that the tension began to mount in Busovaca with the arrival of refugees and displaced from Jajce in December 1992. What did it mean for your municipality? Was it a negligible pressure or was it a major pressure?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: You need to know that into the territory of Busovaca a large number of displaced persons began to arrive. With the arrival of expelled Croats and Bosniaks from the territories of Jajce, the territories then of the Travnik municipality, Kotor Varos, so that we issued an order, because those who had lost their flights were trying at all costs to find another flight, and we tried to prevent that. We prohibited any unlawful entry to flights. So this is this document issued to the military and civilian police to prevent such acts so as -- with a view to avoiding some undesirable circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You're referring to document D263/1?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us, please: I suppose that the Busovaca HVO government was trying to alleviate those tensions in Busovaca, together with Muslim authorities, and there was a meeting between businessmen of Muslim and Croat origin in January to see if they could organise themselves somehow so as to try to ensure life in that area more or less.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had a meeting to see what we could do to receive those poor displaced people arriving from the northern territories of Bosnia and Herzegovina, from where they had been driven away by Serbs, by the Yugoslav and the Serb army, and we tried to accommodate them in a humane, in a manner worthy of man. Because Busovaca, before the war, Busovaca was a tourist resort and there were over 2.000 summer cottages. So we tried to put them up in those cottages so they could live life worthy of human beings, if anything could be called that at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps the time is now to look at the second set of documents, which refers to that period of time when a large number of refugees arrived in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca in November 1992. D264/1, and this is the order of the 19th of November, 1992, you are ordering the civil defence and the chief of the department for national defence to put all units on full alert.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see from the date itself, the 19th of November, the units of the Croat Defence Council and BH army, which had been defending Jajce, had to pull out of the town of Jajce so that all the people from the territory of the municipality of Jajce headed for Busovaca; not only Jajce, but also from Kotor Varos, Jajce, and Dobrovici. And they headed for Busovaca, Vitez, and all the other areas in the Lasva Valley. And we had to prepare everything we could to prepare for themselves everything that they needed so that they could go on with their lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: As you signed the previous document -- not this one, but the one before this one -- and this one, so was it a military order or was it an order of the mayor of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: This was my order, the order, that is, of the civilian mayor of the municipality, because I had to issue such an order to find some roof, some accommodation, for every one of those wretched, of those miserable, of those unfortunate people at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So this is not a military order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: No, this is not a military order; it is my order, issued by me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, you must have been, in your capacity, been involved in plans for the defence of Jajce, defended jointly by the HVO and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Have you ever heard, as it is claimed in this case, that Jajce was handed over, that it fell as a result of some understanding between the HVO and the army of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: I have never heard anything of this sort. I cannot remember exactly, but I know that very many soldiers from Busovaca, the defenders of Jajce, died, and those victims who fell, nobody ever signed such an agreement, nor can I say -- no. I can say that no agreement was ever signed about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The document is now 265/1, another order of yours that you signed on the 19th of November, 1992, and in Article 1 the curfew is imposed for the night hours in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca. Item 2 says that during the curfew only the patrols of the police station of Busovaca, 1, can move in the territory and municipality; that 2, the patrols of HVO, the military police; and 3, the BH army units also allowed to move. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Now, item 4, just a detail. I see that you really thought about every detail very carefully and you said, "Until the time of morning prayer, the mosque is changed. The police patrols shall allow worshippers to attend prayer between ..." so-and-so.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Quite so. We went out of our way not to deprive the Muslims from attending the morning prayer, which is very important for them, and they could attend the Sabah Namaz service every morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And I see you also -- this was, or a copy of this order, was also delivered to the Efendi Prolaz?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Next document, 266/1, another order of yours to the police station in Busovaca to ensure guards around the clock.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a civilian order to ensure the guarding of the municipal hall, the PTT office, the health centre, that is, buildings of vital interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we can agree that all these measures that you are taking go in step with the increase of the crime rate that you felt began to mount in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I need to say here that when the expelled, when the displaced persons arrived from these other territories, that at that time the situation deteriorated. As for the law and order, or rather an increase of the crime rate in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca, because people lacked means of livelihood and they were trying to somehow fend for themselves in all other ways, and I tried to make some law and order there as far as it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The next document is also interesting because it reflects the state of affairs. It's D267/1, of the 24th of November, 1992. You say that the police station in Busovaca is told to control also schools and to search pupils carrying firearms and arms.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, because a very grave problem arose at the time. We observed that even children had some type of ammunition. They began to bring it to school. And there was a boy even who brought a pistol to the school, so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Maric, I think that you simply need to confirm the orders we are speaking of, just by answering Mr. Naumovski's question, without really giving us the details of each particular order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, very briefly, to just go through these few documents which remain. D268/1, this document, if we look at its contents, could fall into that first set of documents. It is dated 25th November, 1992. And in your capacity as the acting mayor of the municipality, that is, president of the HVO government, you take the decision to allow -- entitling Mr. Edim Muminovic to an amount of 300 German marks as damages after an explosive was planted at a kiosk on 2nd November, 1992. This was one of the first outlets which were damaged, and you decided to help the man in some way?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I decided that the man should be helped.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And 269/1, this is your press release of the 8th of December, 1992, which bears on the meeting of HVO representatives in Busovaca with a representative of the Dutch -- UNPROFOR Dutch unit which was stationed there, Mr. De Bur. This document is self-explanatory. However, paragraph 3, the third passage, is interesting. You insisted -- you urged Mr. De Bur to ask through the commander of the UNPROFOR British commander to meet with senior representatives of the HVO and the BH army in order to define the routes and manner of securing humanitarian aid transports and avoid any possible misunderstanding. Evidently you were beginning to have some misgivings about them at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. We can move on to the next document, 270/1. 14th December 1992. I do not think we have to go through it. This is again control of the pupils, once again an appeal to the police.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. D271/1 is a document of the 17th of June, 1993. Item 2 says -- we don't have to go through this document passage by passage, but it has to do with refugees and displaced. But that a commission was set up which allowed those inhabitants who wanted to leave Busovaca and -- it says, I suppose this is your signature down here. We do not have the whole document. The end of the page is missing. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. This is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So in item 3 you're asking the high commander of HVO brigades in Busovaca to issue an order forbidding soldiers to move refugees into anybody's houses on their own initiative, and especially not into Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite so. This is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So this is an attempt of the civilian HVO authority in Busovaca to protect the local population to the maximum possible extent.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Another document in this group, D272/1, of the 21st of June, 1993. This document is self-explanatory, but item 1 is important because in item 1 of this decision, you prohibit the moving out of Muslim families from their homes and the moving in of refugees and displaced persons.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my document of the 21st of June, 1993 in which the persons from -- that is, persons displaced from Zenica tried to move into Muslim houses in Busovaca, and I prohibited this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move on. You also said when Judge Bennouna asked you, you were asked until when did the cooperation last, but it was as late as the 22nd of January, 1993 that you were still distributing food which you were receiving from different humanitarian sources from outside the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and which arrived in Busovaca through the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was some 30 tonnes of food and other aid. Yes, we had obtained food from the Republic of Croatia, and we then distributed it 50/50; that is, half went to Croats and half went to Bosniaks/Muslims, and the remaining Serbs there. So we distributed it equitably and each group distributed it amongst their own population. So that Muslims received 30 tonnes of food on the eve of the conflict; that is, they received it on a Friday and the conflict broke out on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So it was on the eve of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was on the eve of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Shortly after this food distribution, you and Niko Grubesic were invited by Mr. Husein Hadzimejlic to the barracks of the BH army at Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The BH army were quartered in Kacuni, and we went there and we talked because we did not expect -- we could not anticipate the incident which then took place later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What did the barracks look like? Was it already prepared to accommodate a large number of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was organised so as to accommodate a considerable number of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, you communicated with Mr. Hadzimejlic on various occasions. Do you recall if, in late 1992 and early 1993, he told you something about the possibility of controlling radical Muslim soldiers who had arrived in Kacuni from somewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: I can say quite frankly that Mr. Hadzimejlic, who is a wonderful man, who was brought up on religious principles, he always communicated with me and did what he could to ensure good terms, good relations between Croats and Muslims. But with the arrival of displaced persons, especially from Krajina, who were accommodated in the territory of Kacuni and who were, as he put it at times, somewhat bold, right before the conflict broke out he said to me, "Mr. Maric, I can hardly give them any order at all." That is, the situation was very difficult and he simply couldn't keep them under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But before that, and we are referring to paragraph 34, in mid-January 1993, on the 15th, you had a meeting with Dzemal Merdan.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I also had a meeting with Mr. Dzemal Merdan, and an incident then took place in the territory of Kacuni, when a transport -- when a truck with a machine-gun mounted on it patrolled Busovaca and it was stopped at Kacuni. They tried to capture, to seize, this APC, and I asked them to release it, to somehow bring down the tension in order to avoid an incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Tell us, please, prior to the 25th of January, 1993, when the conflict broke out, that is, a few days before that, do you perhaps recall any other incident at Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MARIC
